propositions.text: The claimants are Czech Republic citizens seeking refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).
propositions.quote: The claimants, XXXXXXX ("the principal claimant"), his wife, Jarmila XXXXX ("the female claimant"), XXXXXXXXX (the "daughter" claimant) and her two minor-age children, XXXXXXXXX and XXXXXXXXXXXX (the "minor" claimants) are all citizens of the Czech Republic and they seek refugee protection pursuant to sections 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act1 (the IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The court states the claimants are Czech citizens seeking refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).

propositions.text: Claims were joined under Rule 49(1) of the Refugee Protection Division Rules.
propositions.quote: These claims were joined pursuant to Rule 49(1) of the Refugee Protection Division Rules.

propositions.text: Daughter claimant was designated representative for minor children under section 167(2) of IRPA.
propositions.quote: The daughter claimant, XXXXXXXXX, was the designated representative for the minor children pursuant to section 167(2) of the IRPA.

propositions.text: Principal, female and daughter claimants must rely on each other's testimony to support their claims.
propositions.quote: The Panel is of the opinion that the principal, female and daughter claimants must rely on each other's testimony to support their respective refugee claims.

paragraphs.summary: The Panel joined claims under Rule 49(1), designated daughter claimant as representative, and found claimants must rely on each other's testimony.

propositions.text: All claimants rely on principal claimant's PIF narrative to support their claims.
propositions.quote: The Panel notes that all of the claimants in this proceeding are relying on the PIF narrative of the principal claimant to support their respective claims.

paragraphs.summary: The Panel notes all claimants rely on the principal claimant's PIF narrative to support their claims.

propositions.text: Principal claimant's PIF narrative describes anti-Roma incidents prompting flight from Czech Republic.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant's Personal Information Form (PIF) narrative describes a series of anti-Roma incidents, which were his and his associated family's catalyst to leave the Czech Republic and come to Canada to seek refugee status.

propositions.text: Granddaughter was ostracized, verbally abused, and assaulted at school for being Romani.
propositions.quote: Some of the incidents were briefly described and included the principal claimant's granddaughter being ostracized, verbally abused and assaulted by other children at her school in the Czech Republic for simply being an ethnic Romani.

propositions.text: Female claimant was refused service at hair salon due to no appointment, unlike non-Roma client.
propositions.quote: The female claimant was subjected to discriminatory treatment at a hairdressing salon, where she was refused service because she had no appointment but a non-Roma client was given service.

propositions.text: Female claimant was followed in stores while shopping, which she found demeaning.
propositions.quote: The female claimant was also followed in stores when she was shopping, which she found demeaning.

paragraphs.summary: The principal claimant's PIF describes anti-Roma incidents including granddaughter's abuse, female claimant's discrimination and being followed in stores.

propositions.text: In 2008, principal and female claimants were verbally and physically assaulted by skinheads and reported to police with no response.
propositions.quote: In XXXXXX of 2008, the principal and female claimants were shopping in the town of XXXXX, where they were verbally and physically assaulted by four or five skinheads because of their Roma ethnicity. After this attack, these claimants went to the local police to report this incident and to make a complaint but they never heard back from the police with regard to this incident or the complaint.

propositions.text: In 2008, daughter claimant and boyfriend were attacked by skinheads in a park, reported to police but received no response.
propositions.quote: During a similar incident in XXXX of 2008, the daughter claimant and her boyfriend were verbally and physically attacked in a park by five or six skinheads because of their Roma ethnicity. They did make a police report but they heard nothing back with regard to this incident

paragraphs.summary: In 2008, claimants were attacked by skinheads and reported to police but received no response.

propositions.text: Claimants fear German skinheads and neo-Nazi parties holding rallies near Czech/German border close to their residence.
propositions.quote: The claimants are afraid of the German skinheads and the new neo-Nazi parties that hold rallies and marches near the Czech / German border, which is approximately two kilometres from where the claimants resided.

paragraphs.summary: Claimants fear German skinheads and neo-Nazi rallies near their residence at the Czech/German border.

propositions.text: Claimants left Czech Republic and arrived in Canada in 2009, filing refugee claims at Toronto airport.
propositions.quote: The claimants left the Czech Republic and arrived in Canada on XXXX, 2009, where they filed claims as Convention refugees upon their arrival at the Toronto airport.

paragraphs.summary: Claimants left Czech Republic and filed refugee claims upon arrival in Canada in 2009.

propositions.text: Panel finds claimants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.
propositions.quote: The Panel finds that the claimants are neither Convention refugees nor are they persons in need of protection.

propositions.text: Panel considered credibility, objective reasonableness of fear, discrimination vs persecution, and nexus to Convention refugee definition.
propositions.quote: In arriving at this decision, the Panel has considered the issue of whether the claimants have provided credible and trustworthy evidence and the issue of whether the claimants' fear is objectively reasonable for these specific claimants as it pertains to the issues of discrimination versus persecution and the issue of a nexus to the definition of a Convention refugee.

propositions.text: Panel considered adequacy of state protection, claimant's efforts to seek protection, and evidence of state's inability to protect.
propositions.quote: As well, the Panel has also considered whether or not there is adequate state protection in the Czech Republic, whether the principal claimant took all reasonable steps to avail himself of that protection, and whether he has provided clear and convincing evidence of the state's inability to protect.

paragraphs.summary: The Panel finds claimants are not refugees or in need of protection after considering credibility, fear, discrimination, nexus, and state protection.

propositions.text: Claimants' genuine Czech passports establish their identities as Czech citizens.
propositions.quote: The Panel determines that the claimants' supporting documentation, which includes their genuine Czech passports, establishes their identities as citizens of the Czech Republic.

paragraphs.summary: The Panel finds claimants' genuine Czech passports establish their Czech citizenship.

propositions.text: Credibility is an issue in all IRB claims; claim must be credible on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: Credibility is an issue in all claims before the Immigration and Refugee Board (IRB). In order to determine whether the claim is well-founded, the Panel must find, on a balance of probabilities, that the evidence is credible and trustworthy.

propositions.text: Claimant's testimony presumed true unless valid reasons to doubt truthfulness exist.
propositions.quote: The Panel notes that a claimant's testimony is presumed to be true unless there are valid reasons to doubt its truthfulness.

propositions.text: Contradictions, discrepancies, implausibilities, and omissions justify negative credibility findings.
propositions.quote: The Panel believes that the existence of contradictions, discrepancies, and implausibilities in the evidence of a claimant is a well-accepted basis for a finding of a lack of credibility. This also applies to omissions in the principal claimant's previous statements, whether made to Canadian immigration officials at the time of arrival in Canada, in previous examinations under oath or at the hearing of the claim, or in his PIF.

paragraphs.summary: The Panel explains credibility standards: presumed true unless doubts arise from contradictions or omissions.

propositions.text: Counsel submitted principal claimant's evidence was credible and supported his claim.
propositions.quote: In oral submissions, counsel submitted that the evidence of the principal claimant was credible and that it supported his claim.

propositions.text: Panel disagrees and made negative credibility findings on principal claimant's PIF and oral testimony.
propositions.quote: The Panel does not agree. The Panel drew a number of negative credibility findings with regard to the principal claimant's PIF narrative and his oral testimony and the events that allegedly occurred in the Czech Republic.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel argued principal claimant credible, but Panel disagreed and found negative credibility findings.

propositions.text: Principal claimant testified about 2008 skinhead attack and police report with no follow-up.
propositions.quote: In oral testimony, the principal claimant described the verbal and physical attack by skinheads in XXXXX, which allegedly occurred in XXXXXX of 2008, and his and the female claimant's attendance at the local police station to complain about this incident, where a police report was taken, however, he indicated that the police had never contacted him with regard to this report or any investigation.

propositions.text: Principal claimant said he did not get or request a copy of police report.
propositions.quote: Although a police report was taken with regard to this alleged assault, the principal claimant indicted that he had not been given a copy of this report and he had never requested a copy of this document.

propositions.text: Later, principal claimant contradicted earlier testimony, saying police contacted him and closed case as attackers unknown.
propositions.quote: In later testimony the principal claimant contradicted both his earlier oral testimony and his PIF narrative when he testified that he had been contacted and informed by the police that this matter was now closed because the "persons were unknown."

propositions.text: PIF narrative stated police never responded; principal claimant confirmed this was true.
propositions.quote: The Panel noted the that the principal claimant's PIF narrative states, "We went to the police to make a complaint but we never heard back." The principal claimant confirmed this specific information in his PIF narrative was "true".

propositions.text: Principal claimant later said police sent correspondence closing case a week after incident.
propositions.quote: After a series of questions, the principal claimant changed his testimony, he explained that they had actually been sent correspondence from the police a week after this incident had taken place and that the Czech police had closed this matter because the attackers were "unknown".

paragraphs.summary: Principal claimant gave contradictory testimony about police contact and report regarding 2008 skinhead attack.

propositions.text: Female claimant attempted to prompt principal claimant during testimony about contradictions.
propositions.quote: At this point in the hearing, the Panel noted and observed that the female claimant was attempting to prompt the principal claimant with regard to his testimony pertaining to the contradictions and inconsistencies between his oral testimony and his PIF narrative.

propositions.text: Panel requested female claimant to stop prompting principal claimant.
propositions.quote: The Panel made best efforts to request that the female claimant stop prompting the principal claimant.

paragraphs.summary: Female claimant tried to prompt principal claimant on contradictions; Panel asked her to stop.

propositions.text: Principal claimant admitted receiving police correspondence closing case but left it in Czech Republic and did not bring it.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant was given another opportunity to explain this contradiction and he conceded that he had received police correspondence that the criminal matter was closed. As well, in response to the Panel's questions of why this document was not before it this day, the principal claimant indicated that he had left this specific correspondence in the Czech Republic.

propositions.text: Principal claimant said he was unaware he needed documents to support refugee claim.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant finally indicated that he was not aware that he would need these documents to support his refugee claim.

propositions.text: Panel gives little weight to claimant's explanation given clear PIF instructions and solicitor's likely advice.
propositions.quote: The Panel gives this last explanation little weight since the instructions for question #31 of the PIF narrative are quite clear and they indicate, "On the following two pages, set out in chronological order all the significant events and reasons that have led you to claim refugee protection in Canada. ... Attach copies of any medical, psychological, police or other documents to support your claim." [emphasis within the document]. The principal and other claimants had a previous solicitor, who appears before the IRB on a regular basis and the Panel believes he would be familiar with the instructions for preparing a PIF narrative and the practice of corroborating statements with supporting documents, therefore, it is not reasonable or credible to the Panel that the principal claimant's previous solicitor would not have advised him to obtain any police documents pertaining to this alleged incident in the Czech Republic.

paragraphs.summary: Principal claimant admitted receiving police letter but left it in Czech Republic; Panel disbelieves his excuse given clear instructions and solicitor advice.

propositions.text: Sworn testimony is to be believed without corroboration unless good reason exists not to believe it (Maldonado).
propositions.quote: In Maldonado, the Federal Court stated, "[i]t has long been held that sworn testimony is to be believed, without corroboration, unless there is good reason not to believe it."

propositions.text: UNHCR Handbook states benefit of doubt given only when all evidence obtained and general credibility established.
propositions.quote: According to paragraphs 203 and 204 of the UNHCR Handbook on Procedures and Criteria for Establishing Refugee Status: After the applicant has made a genuine effort to substantiate his story there may still be a lack of evidence for some of his statements. ... it is hardly possible for a refugee to "prove" every part of his case and, indeed, if this were a requirement the majority of refugees would not be recognized. It is therefore frequently necessary to give the applicant the benefit of the doubt. The benefit of the doubt should, however, only be given when all available evidence has been obtained and checked and when the examiner is satisfied as to the applicant's general credibility.

paragraphs.summary: Federal Court and UNHCR rules say sworn testimony is believed unless good reason exists; benefit of doubt requires all evidence obtained and credibility.

propositions.text: Panel cannot give benefit of doubt due to principal claimant's contradictory testimony and lack of efforts to obtain police or medical documents.
propositions.quote: The Panel cannot extend the benefit of the doubt to the principal claimant with regard to his contradictory and inconsistent testimony, which goes directly to the issues of his reliability as a witness and the issues of a lack of state protection by the Czech police. The principal claimant admitted that he made no effort to get this alleged Czech police report, Czech police correspondence or any Czech medical reports with regard to his and his wife's attendance at a the police offices and medical clinic after this alleged attack.

propositions.text: Panel gives little weight to counsel's argument about difficulty obtaining police report given Czech law allows injured party to access documents.
propositions.quote: The Panel gives little weight to counsel's argument that the claimant would have difficulty getting this police report since the documentary evidence that counsel has quoted actually indicates "...according to Criminal Procedures Act No. 141/1961, an "injured party" (or his or her authorized agent or legal representative) has the right to inspect and make copies of all documents in the files of a legal proceeding, except for protected information, such as personal information about witnesses."

propositions.text: Country conditions documentation outlines procedure for obtaining corroborating documents even if injured party is outside Czech Republic.
propositions.quote: In fact, the country-conditions documentation counsel has mentioned actually outlines the procedure for obtaining these corroborating documents even if the "injured party" is not in the Czech Republic.

propositions.text: Principal and female claimants made no concerted efforts to provide reasonably available documentary evidence from Czech Republic.
propositions.quote: For all of these reasons, the Panel determines that the principal and female claimants have not made any concerted efforts to provide documentary evidence from the Czech Republic, which the Panel determines is reasonably available and could have supported these claims.

propositions.text: Panel draws negative credibility finding on principal claimant's oral and documentary evidence.
propositions.quote: For these reasons, the Panel draws a negative credibility finding with regard to the principal claimant's oral and documentary evidence.

paragraphs.summary: Panel finds principal claimant's contradictory testimony and failure to obtain documents undermine credibility; counsel's argument about difficulty is rejected.

propositions.text: Claimants confirmed information was translated before signing declarations; interpreter certified understanding.
propositions.quote: The Panel notes that, during the commencement of the hearing, the principal claimant, female and daughter claimants confirmed that the information had been translated to them before they signed their respective declarations. In fact, the Panel notes that the Czech interpreter, XXXX XXXXX, had indicated with her signature that, "The claimant has indicated that he/she fully understands the entire content of this form and all attached documents and the answers provided, as interpreted by me."

propositions.text: Principal claimant signed PIF indicating information was interpreted and was complete, true and correct.
propositions.quote: In addition, the principal claimant indicated with his own signature and date on the same page of his PIF that the information had been interpreted to him and that it was "complete, true and correct."

propositions.text: Panel gives little weight to daughter claimant's explanation that principal claimant was nervous or confused.
propositions.quote: The Panel gives little weight to the daughter claimant's explanation for the principal claimant's contradictory testimony, which was that he was nervous and may have been confused by the questions, since the Panel gave the principal several opportunities to explain these discrepancies and the Panel asked simple questions, which the principal claimant appeared to understand.

propositions.text: Panel finds principal claimant did not credibly explain contradictions about police contact and is not trustworthy witness on central incident.
propositions.quote: Finally, in assessing this oral testimony, his PIF narrative and his explanations for this contradictory and inconsistent testimony, the Panel determines that the principal claimant has not explained this contradiction that he was never contacted by the police with regard to this police complaint, that his testimony changed or evolved to finally indicate he had been contacted by the Czech police and that he has not been a credible or trustworthy witness with regard to the alleged skinhead attack in the Czech Republic, which was the central incident described in his PIF narrative and a significant catalyst for him and the associated claimants to leave the Czech Republic.

paragraphs.summary: Claimants confirmed translation and understanding; Panel rejects nervousness excuse and finds principal claimant not credible on key incident.

propositions.text: Panel finds on balance of probabilities that alleged 2008 skinhead attack did not occur and was invented by principal claimant.
propositions.quote: In the context of the negative determinations above, the Panel determines, on a balance of probabilities, that the alleged skinhead attack in XXXXX in XXXXXX of 2008 did not take place and has been invented by the principal claimant to support these refugee claims.

propositions.text: Panel draws adverse credibility finding on principal claimant as credible and trustworthy witness.
propositions.quote: For all of the negative determinations noted above, the Panel draws an adverse credibility finding with regard to the principal claimant as a credible and trustworthy witness.

paragraphs.summary: Panel finds alleged 2008 skinhead attack was invented and draws adverse credibility finding on principal claimant.

propositions.text: Claimants' counsel argued claimants have nexus to Convention refugee definition based on race, nationality, or social group as ethnic Romani.
propositions.quote: The claimants' counsel in his oral submissions basically indicated that the claimants have a nexus to the Convention refugee definition of race, nationality, and/or membership in a particular social group as it related to their persecution as an ethnic Romani.

paragraphs.summary: Claimants' counsel argued claimants have nexus to Convention refugee definition as ethnic Romani persecuted.

propositions.text: Panel disagrees with claimants' counsel submissions on nexus to Convention refugee definition.
propositions.quote: The Panel does not agree with these submissions.

paragraphs.summary: Panel disagrees with claimants' counsel submissions on nexus to Convention refugee definition.

propositions.text: About 80,000 Roma live in socially excluded localities in the Czech Republic with limited access to employment, education, housing.
propositions.quote: The documentary evidence shows that an estimated 80,000 of the country's (the Czech Republic) 200,000 to 250,000 Roma inhabit some 300 so-called "socially excluded localities".

propositions.text: Some Czech people, including authorities, discriminate against Roma ethnicity.
propositions.quote: the Panel concludes that some Czech people, including some people in positions of authority, are discriminatory against people of Roma ethnicity.

propositions.text: The principal claimant and female claimant live among general population, work steadily, and have little difficulty finding jobs.
propositions.quote: the principal claimant admitted that he and the female claimant lived among the general Czech population in rented premises, he steadily worked at various positions in the Czech Republic... he had little difficulty finding a job

propositions.text: The daughter claimant secured an apartment and attended trade school but has difficulty finding employment.
propositions.quote: the daughter claimant was able to secure an apartment through her boyfriend's mother and she had been able to attend trade school to XXXXXXXX but she was having difficulty finding employment.

propositions.text: The claimants are exceptions to marginalization or discrimination as they do not live in ghettos and minors attend mainstream schools.
propositions.quote: the claimants before the Panel appear to be exceptions with regard to marginalization or discrimination since these claimants do not live in any Romani ghettos and that the minor claimants... do not attend 'special' Roma schools but they attended mainstream Czech Republic schools.

propositions.text: The specific behaviour towards these claimants does not reach the level of persecution.
propositions.quote: the Panel determines that the specific behaviour towards these claimants does not reach the level of persecution.

propositions.text: Many Roma in Czech Republic are marginalized, under-employed, under-educated, live in subsistence housing, and face violence from radical groups.
propositions.quote: Roma are generally under-employed, under-educated, frequently live in subsistence housing, and are subject to violence from racially motivated radical groups.

propositions.text: These social issues must be viewed in context of the state and its reaction to alleviate discrimination and criminal acts.
propositions.quote: These are complex social issues that must be viewed in the context of the state and its reaction to alleviate such discrimination and criminal acts.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds many Roma marginalized but the claimants are exceptions; some Czech people discriminate against Roma; social issues must be viewed in state context.

propositions.text: The Panel is guided by Supreme Court of Canada and Federal Court cases on state protection principles.
propositions.quote: The Panel, in assessing the issue of state protection, is guided by a number of cases from the Supreme Court of Canada and the Federal Court.

propositions.text: The Panel applies established state protection principles to this case.
propositions.quote: The courts have established a number of principles relating to state protection, and the Panel has applied those principles to the case at bar.

paragraphs.summary: The court applies Supreme Court and Federal Court principles on state protection to this case.

propositions.text: There is a presumption that states can protect citizens except in complete breakdown situations.
propositions.quote: There is a presumption that, except in situations where the state is in complete breakdown, the state is capable of protecting its citizens.

propositions.text: International protection applies only when no other recourse is available to refugee claimants.
propositions.quote: international protection comes into play only when a refugee claimant has no other recourse available.

propositions.text: Claimant bears legal burden to rebut presumption of adequate state protection with clear and convincing evidence.
propositions.quote: the claimant bears the legal burden of rebutting the presumption that adequate state protection exists. To rebut the presumption of state protection, a claimant must provide "clear and convincing" evidence

propositions.text: Evidence of inadequate state protection must be reliable, probative, and satisfy balance of probabilities standard.
propositions.quote: The evidence that state protection is inadequate must not only be reliable and probative, it must also satisfy the Panel, on a balance of probabilities, that state protection is inadequate.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the presumption of state protection and claimant's burden to rebut it with clear, convincing, reliable evidence on balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: Claimants have been provided adequate state protection in Czech Republic.
propositions.quote: The Panel determines that the claimants have been provided with adequate state protection in the Czech Republic.

propositions.text: Principal claimant's alleged 2008 police incident is an invented narrative or lacks corroboration.
propositions.quote: the Panel has determined is an invented narrative

propositions.text: Police took a report and closed investigation due to inability to identify suspects.
propositions.quote: the Czech police on this occasion did take a report and these authorities did indicate by correspondence that the investigation has been closed because the police have not been able to identify these "unknown persons".

propositions.text: It is unreasonable to expect all violent acts reported to police result in prosecutions or convictions.
propositions.quote: it would be unreasonable to expect in any society that all violent acts reported to police would result in immediate prosecutions or convictions.

propositions.text: No corroborating evidence suggests police failed to investigate claimants' allegations genuinely.
propositions.quote: the principal claimant has provided no corroborating information or documents to suggest that police were not making genuine and earnest efforts to investigate

propositions.text: No dated police letter confirms lack of police assistance despite claimants' assertion.
propositions.quote: there is no dated police letter before it to confirm a lack of police assistance, even though the letter was allegedly sent and received by the principal claimant

propositions.text: Claimants failed to provide clear and convincing evidence that state protection is inadequate on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: the claimants have not provided the requisite clear and convincing evidence that, on a balance of probabilities, state protection in the Czech Republic is inadequate.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimants received adequate state protection and failed to prove otherwise with clear, convincing evidence.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence shows Roma face discrimination and violent attacks have declined since 1990s.
propositions.quote: the documentary evidence indicates that the ethnic Romani have faced various forms of discrimination... violent attacks on foreigners and the Roma minority have declined since the 1990s

propositions.text: Judicial proceedings on racial crime have increased due to NGO efforts.
propositions.quote: the judicial proceedings on racial crime have increased in recent years due to the efforts of NGO's.

propositions.text: Societal prejudice against Roma occasionally manifests in violence, mostly by neo-Nazi and ultranationalist groups.
propositions.quote: societal prejudice against the country's Romani population occasionally manifested itself in violence. Members and sympathizers of neo-Nazi organizations were the most frequent perpetrators... ultranationalists were also active.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes Roma face discrimination and violence, but attacks have declined and judicial proceedings increased due to NGO efforts.

propositions.text: Claimants testified skinheads and racist incidents affected them at schools, workplaces, buses, hospitals.
propositions.quote: The principal, female and daughter claimants have testified that their agents of persecution/harm have been at the hands of skinheads but that their family has also been involved in racist incidents at their respective schools, work places, on buses and at hospitals.

propositions.text: State does not condone or acquiesce to racial and discriminatory behavior, especially by extremist groups.
propositions.quote: the state does not condone or acquiesce to this racial and discriminatory behavior, particularly at the hands of extremist skinheads or other fascist groups.

propositions.text: Counsel's submissions about police ignoring two Roma youths' killings in Tanvald are distorted and inaccurate.
propositions.quote: the Panel determines counsel's oral outline of the facts surrounding this incident was actually a distorted opinion of what the Czech authorities are doing.

propositions.text: Authorities investigated the Tanvald incident properly, increased security, and communicated timely information.
propositions.quote: the article indicates that the matter was being investigated properly by the Czech police and the authorities... they did add extra security forces and there were plans to bring in more security / police... the state prosecutor was giving timely information

propositions.text: Another article about a Romani woman murdered in Prague shows police are investigating and charging suspects; attack likely not racially motivated.
propositions.quote: the Panel determines that the Czech police are investigating this incident... this appears to be an attack on homeless people... not a racially motivated attack against Romas... authorities have charged one of the youth with murder

propositions.text: Czech authorities respond properly to attacks against minorities including homeless people.
propositions.quote: the Panel determines that the Czech authorities are responding properly to attacks against other minorites, which includes the homeless in that country.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimants faced racist incidents but state does not condone racism; authorities properly investigate violent incidents.

propositions.text: Since mid-1990s, Czech Ministry of Interior launched anti-extremism initiatives including specialized police departments and specialists.
propositions.quote: In the mid-1990s, the Ministry of the Interior launched an initiative to combat extremism, allowing for police monitoring of extremist group activities... creation of a specialized anti-extremist department... deployment of anti-extremist specialists

propositions.text: There are 130-140 extremist crime investigators nationwide with regional and district assignments.
propositions.quote: there are between 130 and 140 extremist crime investigators across the country, with two members assigned to each region and one to each district.

propositions.text: Anti-extremism offices prevent extremism, work with minorities, raise awareness, and communicate with local authorities.
propositions.quote: The tasks of the various anti-extremism offices... include: preventing and combating extremism and racially motivated crime... working with minority communities... raising awareness in schools; and communicating with local authorities about extremism.

propositions.text: Anti-extremist measures show increasing success according to Ministry of Interior.
propositions.quote: According to the Ministry of the Interior, anti-extremist measures have shown increasing signs of success.

propositions.text: Claimants' counsel's own evidence shows Czech police make significant efforts against neo-Nazis.
propositions.quote: Claimants' counsel's own documentary evidence indicates that the Czech police are making significant efforts to deal with neo-Nazis demonstrating in the country.

propositions.text: Czech authorities are not ignoring racism or allowing it to run unchecked.
propositions.quote: the Czech authorities are not simply sitting on their hands and allowing racism to run rampant or unchecked in the Czech Republic.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Czech government has active anti-extremism initiatives and police efforts against neo-Nazis show success.

propositions.text: Despite challenges, Czech authorities respond adequately to racist violence through legislation and police action.
propositions.quote: the RPD documentary evidence does include examples showing that the authorities... respond adequately to violence by racist Czechs and extremist groups through legislative measures and police action on the ground.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Czech authorities respond adequately to racist violence despite challenges.

propositions.text: State police protection measures include Roma Police Assistants, Minority Liaison Officers, and Anti-Extremism Strategy.
propositions.quote: governmental interlocutors pointed to Roma Police Assistants (RPAs), Minority Liaison Officers (MLOs), and the Ministry of the Interior's Anti-Extremism Strategy.

propositions.text: The Ministry's Strategy on Policing Minorities (2008-2012) includes training, minority employment, crime research, and maintaining RPA and MLO initiatives.
propositions.quote: The Ministry of the Interior's Strategy on Policing Minorities (2008-2012)... includes training on policing minority communities, efforts to employ minorities into the police force, researching crime in socially excluded localities, as well as maintaining the MLO and RPA initiatives.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes police protection measures include RPAs, MLOs, and a policing minorities strategy with training and research.

propositions.text: Holomek believes RPAs would be more effective as police officers; police in Brno prefer RPAs working in NGOs for trust-building.
propositions.quote: Holomek of the SRNM believed that RPAs would be more effective if they were employed as police officers. The police in Brno asserted that having RPAs work in NGOs is better for building trust with Romani communities.

propositions.text: RPA duties include liaising between Roma and police, assisting victims, educating on legal rights, helping investigations, and social services.
propositions.quote: RPA duties include establishing contact between Roma and the police, accompanying Romani victims of crime... educating victims on their legal rights... helping police investigate unreported crime and assisting in the provision of social services in socially excluded localities.

paragraphs.summary: The court describes differing views on RPAs' roles and their duties assisting Roma and police.

propositions.text: NGOs report increased Roma seeking assistance from RPAs, indicating progress and increased trust.
propositions.quote: representatives of DROM... reported that they have seen a general increase in Roma seeking assistance from RPAs.

propositions.text: MLOs help police communicate with minorities and NGOs, participate in social exclusion projects, and improve police-Roma relations.
propositions.quote: MLOs... help introduce police to minority groups and to communicate with NGOs and local authorities... involved in the project "Joint World"... MLO activities had improved communication between police and Roma, contributing to a reduction of crime within Romani communities.

propositions.text: Ministry and NGOs commend MLO effectiveness in crime reduction and community communication.
propositions.quote: Two NGO interlocutors commended the effectiveness of MLOs, and the Ministry of the Interior stated that MLO activities had improved communication between police and Roma, contributing to a reduction of crime within Romani communities.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds NGOs and Ministry commend RPAs and MLOs for improving Roma trust and reducing crime.

propositions.text: Czech government has infrastructure for Roma to seek protection and legal redress if discriminated against or denied security services.
propositions.quote: the Czech government has put in place infrastructure whereby the claimants would have recourse available to seek protection... there is legal redress available if Roma are denied or provided inadequate security services due to their ethnicity.

propositions.text: Citizens can complain about police inaction to the Office of Internal Control by email or phone; complaints are addressed or inspected.
propositions.quote: Citizens can register "complaints about police inaction and non-serious offenses by police officers" with the Office of Internal Control... by sending an email or by contacting by telephone. The complaints will either be immediately addressed or "submitted for inspection"

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Czech government has legal infrastructure for Roma to seek protection and complain about police inaction.

propositions.text: Czech Republic has a Public Defender of Rights (Ombudsman) protecting citizens against improper conduct by authorities.
propositions.quote: the Czech Republic has a Public Defender of Rights - Ombudsman. The Public Defender of Rights is responsible for protecting citizens against the improper conduct of authorities

propositions.text: The Ombudsman has an Equal Treatment Department handling discrimination cases, including about 20% involving Roma.
propositions.quote: the Public Defender "set up a separate Equal Treatment Department... where six staff handle specific cases of... discriminatory practices... Approximately 20 percent of cases handled by this department involve discrimination against Roma.

propositions.text: If complaints fall outside Ombudsman's mandate, complainants are referred to NGOs; complaints are forwarded to responsible units.
propositions.quote: If a complaint does not fall under the mandate... the complainant is provided with contact information for NGOs... if the complaint is submitted to a unit that is not responsible, the unit will pass the complaint to the responsible unit and inform the complainant.

propositions.text: Departments provide protocols and guidance to ensure complaints are properly filed and followed up.
propositions.quote: the various departments outline protocol and provide step-by-step guidance to citizens... to ensure that any complaints are properly filed and registered and, thereafter, followed through by the authorities.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Ombudsman and departments provide discrimination redress and guidance, including referrals to NGOs.

propositions.text: Czech Republic effectively controls its territory and has functioning security forces.
propositions.quote: the Panel determines that the Czech Republic is in effective control of its territory and has in place a functioning security force

propositions.text: Claimants would have recourse to state protection and redress upon return to Czech Republic.
propositions.quote: the claimants... would have recourses available upon their return to the Czech Republic to obtain state protection, and to seek redress if the police were to refuse to respond

propositions.text: Documentary evidence shows Czech Republic's willingness and ability to protect Romani citizens.
propositions.quote: There are numerous examples in the documentary evidence to demonstrate the Czech Republic's willingness and ability to protect its Romani citizens.

propositions.text: Frustration with racial incidents is understandable but no government guarantees perfect protection.
propositions.quote: The Panel understands and sympathizes with the claimants' frustration with regard to racial incidents... no government is expected to guarantee perfect protection to all of its citizens at all times

propositions.text: Less than perfect protection does not mean state is unwilling or unable to offer reasonable protection.
propositions.quote: Less than perfect protection is not a basis to determine that a state is either unwilling or unable to offer reasonable protection.

propositions.text: Police have obligation to protect but cannot guarantee results.
propositions.quote: while police agencies of the state have an obligation to protect, none can ensure the result.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Czech Republic controls territory, offers protection and redress, and less than perfect protection is not failure.

propositions.text: Daughter claimants' children had school problems; societal prejudice against Roma exists.
propositions.quote: The daughter claimants' children have allegedly had problems at school. The Panel acknowledges that societal prejudice against Roma exists in the Czech society

propositions.text: Government is actively engaged in integrating Roma communities into Czech society.
propositions.quote: the government is actively engaged in the integration of the Roma communities in the Czech society.

propositions.text: There is an increasing number of projects supporting preschool and primary education for Roma children.
propositions.quote: there is a continuing increase in the number of supported projects in the key areas of pre-school preparation of Romani children and the education of pupils from the Roma community at primary school.

propositions.text: This trend is positive.
propositions.quote: This trend can be seen as positive.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Roma children face school problems and prejudice but government supports integration and education projects.

propositions.text: There is a targeted program supporting Roma secondary school students to ease financial burdens.
propositions.quote: there is a targeted programme of "Support for Roma Secondary School Students"... supported a total of 2,715 applications in 2007

propositions.text: Support for Roma university students includes development programs and scholarships like Roma Memorial University Scholarship.
propositions.quote: Support for Roma university students is addressed through public university Development Programmes... Roma Memorial University Scholarship awarded by the Roma Educational Fund.

propositions.text: These programs are highly motivational and positive for minor claimants.
propositions.quote: A highly motivational programme is the Roma Memorial University Scholarship...

paragraphs.summary: The court finds targeted programs support Roma secondary and university students, positively aiding minor claimants.

propositions.text: Education levels of Roma are improving, with more attending secondary schools and universities.
propositions.quote: there is a visible trend that shows an improvement in the overall education level of Roma... growing number of pupils and students at secondary schools and universities.

propositions.text: Systematic programs assist Roma integration in mainstream education but are limited by social disadvantage definitions.
propositions.quote: There are systematic programmes of targeted assistance such as preparatory classes, teacher's assistants and projects supporting the integration of Roma into mainstream education; nevertheless, these are limited by the definition of the target group

propositions.text: Roma face social exclusion, national differences, and prejudice, prompting systemic and curricular changes by Ministry.
propositions.quote: Romani children often face not only social exclusion but also national differences and must often deal with the prejudices and stereotypes... the Ministry have started the process of systemic and curricular changes.

propositions.text: Government is addressing discriminatory practices in education and has brought change, though disparities remain.
propositions.quote: the Czech government is continuing to address issues relating to discriminatory practices in education and has brought about change... disparities in education levels continue to exist.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Roma education is improving with government programs, but disparities and prejudice remain.

propositions.text: Government aims to prevent new segregated Roma localities and improve existing ones and housing access.
propositions.quote: the general objective is the endeavour to prevent the establishment of new segregated localities to improve the situation in the already existing segregated Roma localities and to improve access to housing

propositions.text: Socially excluded Roma face low awareness of health prevention; Ministry of Health targets priority areas to improve care.
propositions.quote: socially excluded Roma communities are currently facing a problem of a low level of awareness about the possibilities of health prevention and care. The Czech Ministry of Health has taken steps to target priority areas to improve delivery of health care.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds government aims to improve Roma housing and health care awareness and delivery.

propositions.text: Principal claimant testified main problem is racism from skinheads and racist people in Czech Republic.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant has testified that their main problem is racism from skinheads and racist people in the Czech Republic.

propositions.text: Roma face discrimination and violence from extremist groups but government actively addresses racism through legislation and programs.
propositions.quote: the Panel acknowledges that Roma in the Czech Republic are discriminated against and are victims of violence from extremist groups; however, the Panel finds that the Czech government is actively engaged in addressing racism and racist practices against Roma through legislation, programmes and initiatives

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimants face racism but government actively addresses it through laws and programs.

propositions.text: Czech Republic is a responsible EU member implementing mandated anti-racism standards.
propositions.quote: the Czech Republic is... a responsible member of the European Union and reports regularly to the governance structures within that Union... the Czech Republic is taking the measures to implement the standards that are mandated as a member of the European Union.

propositions.text: Even if criticism is warranted, Czech Republic is making serious efforts to combat racism against Roma.
propositions.quote: Even if criticism of the Czech Republic's measures to combat racism is warranted... the Czech Republic is taking the measures to implement the standards

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Czech Republic is a responsible EU member making serious efforts to combat racism against Roma.

propositions.text: Claimants have not provided clear and convincing evidence that adequate state protection would not be forthcoming upon return to Czech Republic.
propositions.quote: the claimants, in their particular situation and circumstances, have not satisfied the burden by providing clear and convincing evidence that, on a balance of probabilities, adequate state protection would not be reasonably forthcoming if the claimants should need it upon their return to the Czech Republic.

propositions.text: Section 97(1)(b)(iv) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act is relevant to state protection assessment.
propositions.quote: Section 97(1) (b) (iv) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimants failed to prove lack of adequate state protection upon return to Czech Republic, referencing section 97(1)(b)(iv) IRPA.

propositions.text: Claimants need protection because section 97(1)(b)(iv) IRPA is not applicable and Czech health care persecutes Roma due to lower life expectancy.
propositions.quote: counsel has basically submitted that the claimants are in need of protection because section 97(1)(b)(iv) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act is not applicable and the health care system in the Czech Republic persecutes them, due to the fact that the Roma live 14 years less than other Czech nationals.

propositions.text: Covarrubias v. M.C.I. held section 97(1)(b)(iv) is inapplicable if health care is denied on persecutorial grounds.
propositions.quote: counsel cited the decision of Covarrubias, Katia Montano v. M.C.I.34, within which the President of the Court of Appeal... indicated that section 97(1)(b)(iv) is not applicable if the health care is denied to an individual on persecutorial grounds.

propositions.text: Panel finds Covarrubias submission inapplicable here and doubts principal claimant's testimony about 2008 attack; he was satisfied with medical care after.
propositions.quote: The Panel does not find that this submission is applicable in the case at bar... he testified that after this incident he was satisfied with the care he received from the personnel at the medical clinic in XXXXX.

propositions.text: Female and daughter claimants were not satisfied with medical treatment received in Czech Republic.
propositions.quote: both the female and daughter claimants were not satisfied with the medical treatment that had received in their country.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues claimants need protection due to health care persecution; court rejects this, noting principal claimant was satisfied with care but female and daughter were not.

propositions.text: Claimants' documents show poor or denied medical treatment for ethnic Romani, amounting to persecution in health care.
propositions.quote: counsel has referred to the claimants' documentary evidence, which outlines various incidents of poor treatment or denial of medical treatment for ethnic Romani... Romani are persecuted when it comes to health care.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant submits documentary evidence shows Romani face persecution via poor or denied health care.

propositions.text: Panel disagrees with the submission that Romani are persecuted in health care.
propositions.quote: The Panel does not agree.

paragraphs.summary: Court rejects the argument that Romani face persecution in health care.

propositions.text: Roma communities face low awareness of health prevention and care; Czech Ministry of Health is improving health care delivery.
propositions.quote: socially excluded Roma communities are currently facing a problem of a low level of awareness about the possibilities of health prevention and care. The Czech Ministry of Health has taken steps to target priority areas to improve delivery of health care.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Roma face health awareness issues but Czech Ministry of Health is addressing health care delivery.

propositions.text: Report commissioned by World Bank and European Centre details health needs of Roma in Czech and Slovak Republics.
propositions.quote: Within the claimant's own documentary evidence is the report35 of "Health Needs of the Roma Population in the Czech and Slovak Republic...

propositions.text: Report finds lower life expectancy for Roma due to factors like poor hygiene causing diseases, not solely poor medical care.
propositions.quote: there are findings that indicate there is a lower life expectancy for Romas... this fact is actually due to a number of significant factors, which include poor hygiene which leads to diseases such as hepatitis A, parasites, bacteria and viruses and TB36.

propositions.text: Report states one in three hospitalized children under one year old is Roma, though Roma are less than 3% of population.
propositions.quote: one out of every three children under a year old that is hospitalized is Roma, although Roma represent less than 3% of the population.37

propositions.text: Report shows 21.5% prevalence of mental retardation in Roma vs 0.9% non-Roma, partly due to inbreeding and genetic diseases.
propositions.quote: there is a 21.5% prevalence of mental retardation of Roma compared to 0.9% of non Roma; however, the report indicates this is attributable in part due to the problem of inbreeding and also the high prevalence of certain genetic diseases.38

propositions.text: Report mentions unhealthy Roma lifestyle: smoking, poor diet, obesity, alcohol consumption.
propositions.quote: the same report also mentions the unhealthy lifestyle of the Roma including a high prevalence of smoking, low consumption of fruit and vegetables, obesity and consumption of alcohol.39

propositions.text: Report indicates Roma non-compliance with prescribed treatment.
propositions.quote: the report indicated that there was non-compliance with prescribed treatment by the Roma.40

paragraphs.summary: Documentary report details multiple health factors affecting Roma, including hygiene, genetics, lifestyle, and treatment compliance.

propositions.text: Shorter Roma lifespan cannot be attributed to denial of health care on persecutorial grounds; multiple factors contribute.
propositions.quote: the shorter lifespan of the Roma as argued by counsel cannot be attributed to denial of health care to the Roma on persecutorial grounds... several factors as previously mentioned including lifestyle and dietary habits that contribute to their shorter lifespan.

propositions.text: 77% of Roma consider their medical care adequate; claimants would not be denied medical care due to ethnicity.
propositions.quote: 77% of Roma considered the medical care that they and their families received to be adequate... Panel rejects the argument that the claimants would be denied medical care because they are ethnic Romani.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Roma's shorter lifespan is due to multiple factors, not health care denial; majority consider medical care adequate, rejecting denial claim.

propositions.text: Principal claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection under sections 96 or 97 IRPA; negative finding extends to female, daughter, and minor claimants.
propositions.quote: the principal claimant is not a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection, whether under section 96 or section 97 of the IRPA. This negative determination extends to the female, daughter and minor claimants...

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes principal claimant and dependents are not refugees or in need of protection under IRPA sections 96 or 97.

propositions.text: Refugee Protection Division rejects all claims of the claimants.
propositions.quote: The Refugee Protection Division rejects all of these respective claims.

paragraphs.summary: Refugee Protection Division rejects all claimants' claims.
